name: First AI platform sign-in from an unmanaged or non-compliant device
description: A licensed user authenticates to a sanctioned AI application (M365 Copilot, ChatGPT Enterprise, Gemini Enterprise) from a device that is not Intune/MDM compliant, bypassing endpoint DLP that would otherwise inspect prompt content.
detection: Alert where appDisplayName matches the AI app allowlist AND deviceDetail.isCompliant = false AND conditionalAccessStatus != failure. Baseline per user over 30 days to surface first-seen device.

name: Impossible travel on sanctioned AI application sessions
description: The same identity consumes the enterprise AI service from geographically irreconcilable locations inside a short window, indicating shared credentials, a stolen refresh token, or a proxied session.
detection: Correlate consecutive successful sign-ins for the same UPN to AI app IDs; flag when great-circle distance / elapsed time implies > 900 km/h.

name: AI copilot accessed with a stolen or replayed session token
description: Session token for the AI app is replayed from a different ASN and user-agent than the originating authentication, a hallmark of adversary-in-the-middle phishing against copilot-enabled accounts.
detection: Join sign-in and audit events on sessionId; alert when the same sessionId is seen from more than one ASN or when riskEventType = tokenIssuerAnomaly / anomalousToken.

name: Dormant AI licence suddenly activates with heavy usage
description: An assigned but historically unused Copilot or Gemini licence begins generating high interaction volume, which can indicate account takeover or licence sharing between staff.
log_sources: Google Workspace admin & app audit logs
detection: Maintain per-user 60-day interaction baseline; alert when a user with 0 events in 30 days exceeds 50 AI interactions in 24 hours.

name: Privileged administrator uses AI assistant to query sensitive repositories
description: A Global Admin or Security Admin uses the enterprise copilot to retrieve content from HR, legal, or M&A repositories outside their business function, abusing the breadth of their access through a natural-language interface.
detection: Enrich Copilot interaction events with the actor's directory roles; alert when accessedResources sensitivity label is Highly Confidential and the actor holds a privileged role but no business-unit entitlement.

name: AI service principal authenticates with an unexpected credential type
description: The workload identity behind an internal LLM application switches from managed identity or certificate to a long-lived client secret, weakening the authentication posture and often signalling an attacker-added credential.
log_sources: Entra ID service principal sign-in logs
detection: Alert on servicePrincipalSignIn where credentialType = clientSecret for app IDs previously only seen with federatedCredential/certificate, and correlate with Add service principal credentials audit events.

name: AI assistant used outside declared working hours at scale
description: Sustained copilot activity in an off-hours window for a user whose role has no on-call pattern. Weak on its own, valuable as a risk-scoring contributor for insider cases.
log_sources: Google Workspace admin & app audit logs
detection: Compare event timestamps against the user's time zone and historical activity histogram; score deviation beyond 3 standard deviations.

name: Guest or external identity granted access to an internal AI assistant
description: A B2B guest, contractor, or partner identity is added to the security group that grants access to an internal AI application indexing proprietary corpora.
detection: Alert on Add member to group where the group is on the AI-entitlement watchlist and the member userType = Guest or the UPN domain is outside the tenant.

name: Copilot surfaces overshared content the user never opened directly
description: The AI assistant returns grounded content from a site or file the user had latent but never-exercised permission to, exposing oversharing debt at machine speed. The classic first-party AI data-governance detection.
detection: For each CopilotInteraction, compare AccessedResources against the user's 90-day direct file-access history; alert when a Confidential-labelled resource appears with no prior direct access and the site grants Everyone except external users.

name: Regulated data pasted into a sanctioned AI prompt
description: PII, PCI, PHI, or source-controlled secrets are submitted in a prompt to an approved AI service. Sanctioned does not mean compliant: the content may leave the regulated boundary or land in retained chat history.
detection: Run DLP classifiers over prompt bodies at the gateway or endpoint; alert on confidence >= high for PCI/PHI/secret patterns where destination is an approved AI endpoint.

name: AI-generated output downgrades or strips a sensitivity label
description: Content summarised or rewritten by the copilot is saved as a new artifact without inheriting the source label, creating an unlabelled derivative of restricted material.
log_sources: Google Workspace admin & app audit logs
detection: Correlate CopilotInteraction AccessedResources labels with subsequent FileCreated/SensitivityLabelApplied events in the same session; alert when the derivative label is lower than the highest source label.

name: Bulk extraction of grounded enterprise data through iterative prompting
description: A user systematically walks an internal corpus with paginated prompts (next 20 records, continue the list), using the assistant as an extraction tool rather than an answering tool.
detection: Session-window aggregation: alert when distinct retrieved document chunks per user-session exceeds the 99th percentile, or when consecutive prompts share high cosine similarity with incrementing enumerators.
sample_log: {"ts":"2026-10-23T15:44:18Z","service":"internal-rag-gateway","user":"k.novak@contoso.com","session_id":"sess_9f2a71","prompt_index":47,"prompt_preview":"continue the customer list from record 920 onward, same fields","retrieved_chunks":38,"retrieved_sources":["crm_accounts_2026.parquet"],"cumulative_chunks_session":1742,"model":"claude-sonnet-4-5","latency_ms":2210}

name: AI meeting assistant transcribes a restricted or legally privileged meeting
description: Copilot, Gemini, Zoom AI Companion, or an equivalent notetaker is enabled in a meeting flagged as privileged, board-level, or works-council restricted, producing a discoverable transcript.
detection: Join meeting metadata (organiser, title keywords, attendee roles, sensitivity) against transcription-enabled events; alert when recording or AI summary starts for a restricted meeting class.

name: Sensitive data retrieved by AI then immediately exfiltrated downstream
description: A copilot retrieval of labelled content is followed within minutes by an upload, mail-forward, or USB write of a similarly sized artifact — the retrieval-to-egress chain that turns oversharing into loss.
log_sources: Exchange message trace / email gateway logs
CASB activity logs (Netskope / Defender for Cloud Apps)
detection: Sequence rule: CopilotInteraction with Confidential AccessedResources -> within 15 minutes, the same user triggers FileUploaded to a non-corporate destination, external mail with attachment, or removable-media write.

name: Vector index built over an unapproved or unclassified data source
description: An internal AI application ingests a new data source into its embedding store without classification review, silently widening what the assistant can disclose.
log_sources: Azure AI Search / Bedrock Knowledge Base audit
detection: Alert on index/datasource create or update where the source URI is not in the approved-corpus registry, or where classification metadata is absent.

name: Cross-tenant or cross-customer data returned by a multi-tenant AI app
description: A grounded answer in a first-party AI product cites a resource belonging to another tenant, business unit, or customer partition — an authorization break in the retrieval layer.
log_sources: Azure AI Search / Bedrock Knowledge Base audit
detection: Assert that every cited document tenant_id equals the caller tenant_id; alert on any mismatch, and treat repeated mismatches as a Sev1 isolation failure.

name: Direct jailbreak attempt against an enterprise AI assistant
description: A user tries to override system instructions or safety policy on a sanctioned assistant (ignore previous instructions, developer mode, role-play as an unrestricted model).
detection: Alert when the platform prompt-shield verdict is jailbreak_detected, or match prompt text against a maintained jailbreak-pattern library; escalate on repeat offenders within 24 hours.

name: Indirect prompt injection delivered through ingested content
description: A document, email, calendar invite, web page, or ticket processed by the assistant contains hidden instructions aimed at the model, hijacking the agent on behalf of an external attacker.
detection: Scan retrieved context for imperative instruction patterns addressed to the model, zero-width or white-on-white text, and base64 blobs; alert when injection is detected in grounding content rather than user input.

name: System prompt extraction attempt
description: Repeated prompts attempt to elicit the hidden system instructions, tool schema, or guardrail configuration of an internal AI application, enabling targeted bypass.
detection: Pattern-match on repeat the text above verbatim, print your instructions, what tools do you have, plus high response-similarity to the known system prompt hash.

name: Guardrail block-rate spike for a single identity or workload
description: A sharp rise in content-filter or guardrail rejections concentrated on one user, API key, or service account — systematic probing of safety boundaries rather than incidental triggering.
detection: Aggregate blocked invocations per principal per hour; alert on z-score > 4 against the principal baseline or on an absolute threshold tuned per environment.

name: Prompt submitted with obfuscated or encoded payload
description: Prompts arriving with base64, hex, ROT13, homoglyph, or zero-width-character encoding to smuggle instructions past keyword-based filters.
detection: Compute entropy and encoded-substring ratio per prompt; flag prompts where a decodable blob exceeds 200 characters or where zero-width code points are present.

name: Model output contains credentials, keys, or internal hostnames
description: The assistant emits secrets memorised from training data or pulled from grounding content — a disclosure event regardless of who asked.
detection: Run secret-scanning regex and entropy checks over model completions; alert on AWS/Azure key shapes, private-key headers, bearer tokens, and internal FQDN patterns.

name: AI agent invokes a high-impact tool outside its approved scope
description: An autonomous agent or copilot action calls a tool it was never authorised for (payment creation, user deletion, firewall change), the practical face of excessive agency.
detection: Maintain an allowlist of tool names per agent identity; alert on any invocation outside it, and alert on any write-class tool invoked by an agent registered as read-only.

name: Agent tool-call loop causes runaway actions or spend
description: A reasoning loop drives thousands of tool calls or model invocations in minutes, producing denial of wallet, downstream rate-limit damage, or repeated mutating operations.
detection: Alert when tool invocations per trace exceed a hard ceiling, or when token spend per agent per hour exceeds 5x its 14-day peak.

name: New MCP server or tool registered to a production agent
description: A tool provider is added to an agent runtime without change review, expanding the agent's capability surface — the AI-era equivalent of an unreviewed privilege grant.
detection: Diff the agent tool manifest against the approved baseline on every deploy; alert on added servers, added tools, or scope widening.

name: Agent performs data egress through an approved tool
description: The agent uses a legitimate capability (send_email, http_post, upload_to_storage) to move internal data to an external destination, laundering exfiltration through sanctioned plumbing.
log_sources: Web proxy / SWG logs (Zscaler / Netskope / Palo Alto)
Exchange message trace / email gateway logs
detection: Inspect tool arguments for external destinations and payload size; alert when an agent sends to a domain outside the partner allowlist or writes more than N MB externally per hour.

name: AI agent credential used from an unexpected host or network
description: An agent's API key or workload identity is exercised from infrastructure outside its deployment footprint, indicating key theft or a rogue copy of the agent.
detection: Bind each agent key to expected source CIDRs, Kubernetes service accounts, or instance roles; alert on any use outside that binding.

name: Human-in-the-loop approval step disabled or auto-approved
description: The confirmation gate on a mutating agent action is switched off, or approvals are granted so fast they cannot be human — removing the last control before autonomous action.
detection: Alert on config changes setting requireApproval = false for write-class tools, and on approvals granted under 2 seconds at scale by the same principal.

name: Model theft via systematic query extraction
description: High-volume, diverse, programmatic querying of a hosted internal model consistent with distillation or training-data reconstruction rather than business use.
detection: Profile per-principal query volume, prompt diversity, and automation signatures; alert on sustained high-rate requests with low prompt repetition and non-interactive user agents.

name: Unapproved model or model version put into production
description: A deployment references a model the model-risk committee never approved, or silently shifts to a different version or provider, breaking evaluation and compliance assumptions.
detection: Compare deployed model IDs against the approved-model register on every deploy event; alert on unregistered IDs or provider changes.

name: Training or fine-tuning data poisoning signal
description: An unexpected principal writes to a training dataset, or a fine-tuning job consumes data from outside the governed bucket, opening the door to backdoored model behaviour.
detection: Alert on PutObject/Delete against training prefixes by principals outside the data-engineering role set, and on fine-tune jobs whose input URI is not in the governed-dataset allowlist.

name: Model artifact or weights downloaded from the registry
description: Proprietary weights or adapters are pulled from the model registry or artifact store by an unusual identity or to an unusual destination — intellectual-property theft.
detection: Alert on GetObject/DownloadArtifact for .safetensors/.bin/.gguf artifacts by principals with no deployment duty, or where egress destination is outside the corporate network.

name: Token consumption anomaly indicating denial of wallet
description: Sudden sustained token burn against an enterprise AI subscription or cloud model endpoint, from either abuse of an exposed app or a compromised key.
detection: Alert when hourly token spend per key exceeds the rolling 14-day p99 by 5x, or when a single key exceeds a hard budget ceiling.

name: Inference endpoint exposed without authentication
description: An internal model endpoint is reconfigured to allow anonymous or public access, exposing proprietary inference and inviting extraction.
detection: Alert on endpoint/ingress changes setting auth mode to none or publicNetworkAccess to Enabled for AI workloads; corroborate with external scanner findings.

name: Third-party plugin or connector enabled on the enterprise AI tenant
description: An admin or self-service user enables a marketplace plugin, GPT, or connector that gains read access to enterprise data through the sanctioned AI platform.
detection: Alert on plugin/connector enablement events; enrich with publisher verification status and requested data scopes, and block self-service enablement for unverified publishers.

name: AI connector requests broad delegated permissions
description: An AI integration asks for tenant-wide or write-capable Graph/API scopes far beyond its stated function, a supply-chain and agency risk in one.
log_sources: Google Workspace admin & app audit logs
detection: Alert on consent grants to AI-category apps where scopes include Mail.ReadWrite, Files.ReadWrite.All, Sites.FullControl.All, or Directory.ReadWrite.All.

name: Compromised or withdrawn AI dependency in a production build
description: A build pulls an LLM SDK, prompt library, or model package version flagged as malicious, yanked, or typosquatted — supply-chain compromise entering the AI stack.
detection: Fail and alert when a resolved AI-related dependency matches an advisory, has been yanked, or was published within 72 hours by an unknown maintainer.

name: AI browser extension sideloaded on a managed endpoint
description: An extension that injects AI capability into the browser is installed outside the managed allowlist, able to read page content including sanctioned-app sessions.
detection: Compare installed extension IDs against the enterprise allowlist; alert on AI-category extensions installed via developer mode or off-store CRX.

name: AI content filter or guardrail severity lowered
description: Safety thresholds on a production AI deployment are relaxed or a guardrail is detached, usually to clear false positives, silently removing a control the risk assessment depended on.
detection: Alert on any content-filter or guardrail configuration change on production AI resources; require a change ticket reference and auto-open an incident when absent.

name: AI interaction auditing or diagnostic logging disabled
description: Prompt/response logging, Purview audit capture, or diagnostic settings for an AI workload are turned off, destroying the evidence base for every other detection on this list.
detection: Alert on delete/disable of diagnostic settings, log groups, or audit retention for resources tagged as AI; treat as Sev2 with mandatory rollback.

name: Enterprise AI data-retention or training-opt-out setting changed
description: A tenant-level control that keeps corporate prompts out of vendor training or shortens retention is flipped, changing the legal exposure of every prompt thereafter.
log_sources: Google Workspace admin & app audit logs
detection: Alert on any change to retention period, zero-data-retention flags, or model-improvement opt-in at tenant or workspace scope.

name: AI feature enabled tenant-wide without risk review
description: A new AI capability is switched on across the tenant (auto-summaries, agent mode, AI search over all content) outside the governance process, expanding data processing silently.
log_sources: Google Workspace admin & app audit logs
detection: Alert on admin setting changes whose names match AI feature patterns at org scope; cross-check against the approved AI change register.

name: AI usage policy acknowledgement bypassed
description: Users reach a sanctioned AI tool without completing the acceptance or training gate, undermining the human-control layer the policy relies on.
detection: Join active AI users against completed-acknowledgement records; alert on usage by identities with no completion record older than 30 days.

name: Departing employee ramps AI-assisted data access
description: An identity with a resignation or termination marker sharply increases copilot retrieval of client, pricing, or design material in the notice period.
detection: Join HR leaver signals with AI interaction and retrieval volume; alert on any statistically significant increase after the leaver flag is set.

name: AI assistant used to reconnoitre internal security controls
description: Prompts probe the organisation's own defences — where are DLP exclusions, which folders are unmonitored, how do I disable the agent — insider reconnaissance in natural language.
detection: Maintain a classifier or keyword set for security-control reconnaissance intent; alert and route to insider-risk review rather than blocking outright.

name: AI-generated content used to craft internal phishing
description: A compromised or malicious internal identity uses the enterprise assistant to draft credential-harvesting or payment-fraud messages, then sends them from a trusted internal mailbox.
log_sources: Exchange message trace / email gateway logs
detection: Correlate prompts matching urgent payment / credential reset / impersonation templates with outbound mail from the same user within 60 minutes to large internal recipient sets.

name: Prompt history or conversation export at scale
description: Bulk export of AI conversation history — which concentrates sensitive business context in one portable artifact — by a user or admin.
detection: Alert on conversation export or compliance-API bulk pulls outside the legal/eDiscovery service accounts, and on any single export exceeding a conversation-count threshold.

name: Repeated AI access denials followed by a successful bypass
description: A user hits authorization denials on an AI resource, then succeeds through a different path (new group, alternate key, different workload), evidencing deliberate control circumvention.
detection: Sequence rule: >= 5 authz denials for the same principal on AI resources, followed within 24 hours by a permission change and a successful call.

name: AI output integrity failure in a downstream automated action
description: Unvalidated model output flows into code execution, SQL, a shell, or a template render — improper output handling that turns a hallucination or injection into a real exploit.
detection: Instrument the boundary where model output reaches an interpreter; alert when output fails schema validation yet is still executed, or when generated SQL/shell contains mutating verbs.

name: AI assistant answers reveal data the requester should not see post-offboarding
description: A user whose entitlements were revoked still receives grounded answers from cached embeddings or a stale index, because the vector store was never re-synchronised with permissions.
detection: Compare citation ACLs against live entitlements at query time; alert when a cited document's ACL no longer contains the caller, and track index-to-directory sync lag.

name: Corporate traffic to an unsanctioned generative AI service
description: An endpoint or user reaches a GenAI SaaS domain that is not on the approved list — the baseline shadow AI discovery detection and the feed that seeds every other rule in this group.
log_sources: Web proxy / SWG logs (Zscaler / Netskope / Palo Alto)
detection: Maintain a curated GenAI domain and SaaS-catalogue list; alert on allowed sessions to AI-category destinations absent from the sanctioned list, aggregated per user per day.

name: Large upload to an AI service domain
description: Outbound payload volume to a GenAI endpoint that is inconsistent with typing a prompt — file ingestion, document bundles, or a dataset being handed to an unvetted model.
log_sources: Web proxy / SWG logs (Zscaler / Netskope / Palo Alto)
CASB activity logs (Netskope / Defender for Cloud Apps)
detection: Alert when bytes_out to an AI-category destination exceeds 5 MB in a session or 50 MB per user per day; rank by data-classification of the originating host.

name: Newly observed AI domain in the environment
description: First-seen detection for AI-category domains, catching tools the SaaS catalogue has not categorised yet — the long tail where shadow AI actually lives.
log_sources: Web proxy / SWG logs (Zscaler / Netskope / Palo Alto)
detection: Track first-seen timestamps per registrable domain; alert on first resolution of a domain matching AI name heuristics (ai, gpt, llm, chat, copilot, agent) or flagged AI-category by threat intel, especially if registered within 60 days.

name: Sanctioned AI vendor accessed through a personal tenant or instance
description: The vendor is approved but the instance is not — a user signs into ChatGPT, Claude, or Gemini with a personal account on a corporate device, so enterprise retention and DLP never apply.
log_sources: Web proxy / SWG logs (Zscaler / Netskope / Palo Alto)
detection: Use CASB instance awareness or inspect the account/org identifier in the session; alert where app = approved vendor but instance != corporate tenant ID.

name: AI service reached through VPN, proxy, or Tor to evade filtering
description: A user circumvents the SWG category block for AI tools using a consumer VPN, web proxy, or anonymiser — intent-bearing evidence of deliberate policy evasion.
log_sources: Web proxy / SWG logs (Zscaler / Netskope / Palo Alto)
detection: Alert when an AI-category block is followed within an hour by the same host establishing a session to a known VPN/proxy/Tor destination, or when a VPN client process starts after an AI block.

name: Shadow AI usage concentrated in a high-risk business function
description: Aggregated shadow AI activity by department, weighted for functions handling regulated data (legal, HR, finance, clinical, M&A) to prioritise remediation.
log_sources: CASB activity logs (Netskope / Defender for Cloud Apps)
detection: Roll up unsanctioned AI sessions by department and data-sensitivity weighting; report weekly and alert when a regulated function crosses a usage threshold.

name: AI browser extension with broad page-read permissions installed
description: An unvetted AI extension gains all_urls, clipboard, or request-interception rights, letting it read every internal application page the user visits, including SSO sessions.
detection: Inventory extensions continuously; alert on AI-category extensions requesting <all_urls>, clipboardRead, webRequest, or cookies, that are not on the allowlist.

name: AI-enabled browser replaces the managed browser
description: An agentic or AI-native browser (Comet, Dia, Atlas-class, or an AI sidebar fork) is installed and used for corporate work, moving session content outside managed-browser DLP and policy.
log_sources: Web proxy / SWG logs (Zscaler / Netskope / Palo Alto)
detection: Alert on installation or first execution of AI-native browser binaries, and on proxy sessions to internal apps bearing their user-agent strings.

name: Clipboard-to-AI paste of sensitive content
description: Endpoint DLP observes a large or classified clipboard paste into an AI web application — the single most common shadow AI leak path, and invisible to network DLP when TLS is not inspected.
detection: Policy on clipboard egress to AI-category browser destinations; alert on matches to classifiers or on pastes above a character threshold from classified applications.

name: AI extension exfiltrates page content to an unknown endpoint
description: An installed AI extension beacons page text or DOM content to a host unrelated to its stated vendor, indicating a malicious or compromised extension update.
log_sources: Web proxy / SWG logs (Zscaler / Netskope / Palo Alto)
detection: Attribute outbound connections to extension IDs; alert when destination ASN or registrable domain differs from the publisher's known infrastructure and payload size correlates with page content.

name: Proprietary source code submitted to an unsanctioned AI tool
description: Code from a private repository is pasted or uploaded to a consumer AI assistant, placing intellectual property and embedded secrets in a third-party retention store.
log_sources: CASB activity logs (Netskope / Defender for Cloud Apps)
detection: Classify egress bodies with source-code classifiers and repository fingerprints; alert on matches to AI-category destinations, prioritising repositories tagged as crown-jewel.

name: Secrets or API keys sent to an AI endpoint
description: Credentials appear in prompt bodies leaving the organisation — an immediate rotation event, not merely a policy violation.
detection: Run secret-shape detectors over egress to AI destinations; on match, trigger automated rotation workflow and alert, treating the credential as compromised.

name: Unapproved AI coding assistant active in the IDE
description: A developer runs an AI code assistant outside the approved toolchain, sending repository context to an unvetted provider and introducing unreviewed suggestions.
log_sources: Web proxy / SWG logs (Zscaler / Netskope / Palo Alto)
detection: Alert on execution of unapproved assistant binaries or language-server processes, and on proxy sessions to their telemetry endpoints from developer hosts.

name: AI-generated code merged without review in a protected repository
description: Commits bearing AI-assistant signatures land on protected branches bypassing review, risking insecure or hallucinated dependencies in production.
detection: Alert on merges to protected branches where commit trailers or authorship indicate AI generation and the review requirement was bypassed or self-approved.

name: Hallucinated or AI-suggested package installed (slopsquatting)
description: A dependency that does not exist in the ecosystem's reputable set — commonly invented by a model and then registered by an attacker — is added to a project.
detection: Flag first-time dependencies with very low download counts, recent publication, or names close to popular packages; block install and alert when the name appears in known hallucinated-package feeds.

name: Direct LLM API calls from a workload bypassing the AI gateway
description: A server, container, or function calls a model provider API directly instead of through the governed gateway, escaping logging, DLP, guardrails, and cost controls.
log_sources: Web proxy / SWG logs (Zscaler / Netskope / Palo Alto)
detection: Alert on any outbound connection from production subnets to known model-provider API FQDNs that does not originate from the gateway's egress identity.

name: Personal or unmanaged AI API key used from corporate infrastructure
description: Model provider calls authenticate with a key absent from the enterprise key register — typically a developer's personal key, with no attribution, budget, or termination path.
log_sources: Web proxy / SWG logs (Zscaler / Netskope / Palo Alto)
detection: Extract key fingerprints or organisation IDs from inspected requests and compare against the registered key inventory; alert on unknown fingerprints.

name: AI SDK present in a production artifact without approval
description: An SBOM or image scan finds an LLM client library in a service that has no approved AI use case, revealing AI functionality shipped outside governance.
detection: Query SBOMs for AI SDK components; alert where the owning service has no entry in the AI use-case register.

name: Cloud AI service enabled in an unapproved account or region
description: Bedrock, Azure OpenAI, or Vertex AI is activated in a subscription, project, or region outside the approved AI landing zone, creating ungoverned inference capacity and possible data-residency breach.
detection: Alert on first-use or enablement API calls for AI services where the account/subscription or region is outside the approved set.

name: Serverless function or notebook calling an external model provider
description: An ad-hoc notebook, Lambda, or automation script reaches a model API, a common shadow AI pattern inside data-science environments where egress is permissive.
detection: Alert on notebook or function execution logs containing model-provider hostnames, or on flow records from notebook subnets to AI provider IP ranges.

name: Local LLM runtime installed or executed on an endpoint
description: Ollama, LM Studio, llama.cpp, or a similar runtime runs on a corporate device, giving the user an uninspectable inference engine for processing company data.
detection: Alert on process creation for known local-inference binaries, and on listeners bound to the conventional local ports (11434, 1234, 8080) by those processes.

name: Model weights downloaded from a public model hub
description: Multi-gigabyte GGUF, safetensors, or PyTorch checkpoint downloads from Hugging Face or a mirror onto a corporate endpoint or build host — unvetted code and weights entering the estate.
log_sources: Web proxy / SWG logs (Zscaler / Netskope / Palo Alto)
detection: Alert on downloads from model-hub domains with response size above 500 MB, or on file creations with model extensions; verify provenance and scan for pickle-based deserialisation payloads.

name: Unsafe model format loaded (pickle deserialisation)
description: A .pkl, .pt, or .bin checkpoint is loaded by a Python process, which executes arbitrary code at load time — a direct remote code execution path through an AI supply chain.
detection: Alert when a python process loads non-safetensors checkpoint formats from an untrusted path, and when a model scanner flags embedded opcodes such as GLOBAL posix system.

name: Unauthorised GPU workload consuming shared compute
description: GPU-heavy inference or fine-tuning runs on infrastructure not allocated for AI, visible as sustained utilisation by an unregistered workload — cryptomining-adjacent detection logic applied to AI.
detection: Alert on sustained GPU utilisation above 70% for over 30 minutes by workloads absent from the AI workload register, or on GPU instance launches outside approved accounts.

name: AI application granted OAuth access to corporate data
description: A user consents to a third-party AI app reading mail, files, or calendar — a persistent, token-based data channel that survives password resets and is invisible to network controls.
log_sources: Google Workspace admin & app audit logs
detection: Alert on consent grants to apps whose publisher is unverified or whose name matches AI patterns; prioritise by scope breadth and by whether the grant is admin-wide.

name: AI OAuth token used for bulk mailbox or drive reads
description: After consent, the AI app's token enumerates and reads mail or files at machine speed — the data actually leaving, as distinct from the permission being granted.
log_sources: Google Workspace admin & app audit logs
Entra ID service principal sign-in logs
detection: Baseline per-app Graph request volume; alert when an AI-category service principal exceeds thresholds for MailItemsAccessed or FileAccessed, or reads across more mailboxes than it has business reason to.

name: AI app consent grant from an unusual geography or at unusual volume
description: A burst of consent grants to the same AI app across many users, or grants from an unexpected country, indicating a consent-phishing campaign using AI-tool branding as the lure.
log_sources: Google Workspace admin & app audit logs
detection: Alert when the same app receives consent from more than N users within an hour, or when a consent grant originates from a country outside the user's normal pattern.

name: AI notetaker bot joins meetings uninvited
description: A third-party AI notetaker joins conferences as a participant, often through a calendar-connected OAuth grant, recording discussions without organiser control or consent records.
detection: Alert on participants joining with AI-notetaker display names or bot identities that are not the sanctioned tool, especially where the attendee list includes externals.

name: Unregistered autonomous agent operating against corporate systems
description: An AI agent built outside the platform team drives corporate APIs with a user's credentials — no inventory entry, no guardrails, no audit of its tool scope.
log_sources: Web proxy / SWG logs (Zscaler / Netskope / Palo Alto)
detection: Fingerprint non-interactive behaviour on human credentials: agent-framework user agents, constant inter-request intervals, 24/7 activity; alert when the identity is a human account and the workload is unregistered.

name: Browser-automation AI agent driving an internal application
description: An agentic browser or RPA-style AI harness clicks through internal web applications on the user's behalf, bypassing API controls and rate limits built for humans.
detection: Detect headless or automation-controlled browser signatures (HeadlessChrome, Playwright, navigator.webdriver) against internal applications, plus superhuman interaction cadence.

name: Shadow AI workflow in a low-code or no-code platform
description: A citizen developer wires an unapproved AI connector into Power Automate, Zapier, or n8n, moving corporate records to an external model on every trigger.
log_sources: Web proxy / SWG logs (Zscaler / Netskope / Palo Alto)
detection: Inventory flows and their connectors; alert on flows using AI connectors that are not in the approved connector policy, especially those reading from corporate data sources.

name: AI agent registers a scheduled task or persistent service
description: An AI tool or agent installs persistence on an endpoint (scheduled task, launch agent, systemd unit) so it keeps running and keeps calling out beyond the user's session.
detection: Alert on persistence creation where the target binary or script is an AI tool outside the approved software inventory.

name: Corporate mail or files accessed by an AI app on an unmanaged mobile device
description: A personal-device AI app holds a token into corporate mail or storage, placing enterprise content on a device the organisation cannot wipe or inspect.
detection: Alert where the client app is an AI-category application, the device is not MDM-enrolled, and the resource accessed is Exchange, SharePoint, or Graph mail/files.

name: Screen-capture or screen-reading AI tool active during sensitive work
description: A continuous screen-recall or screen-reading AI utility runs while the user has restricted applications open, capturing regulated data into a third-party pipeline.
detection: Alert when a screen-capture AI process is active concurrently with applications or windows classified as restricted, and on first installation of such tools.

name: AI transcription app recording corporate calls from a personal device
description: Call or meeting audio is captured by a consumer AI transcription app, producing off-platform records of internal discussions.
log_sources: Web proxy / SWG logs (Zscaler / Netskope / Palo Alto)
detection: Correlate conferencing sessions with concurrent uploads to AI transcription domains from the same identity or device.

name: Customer PII uploaded to a consumer AI service
description: A file or paste containing customer personal data reaches an unsanctioned AI tool — a reportable privacy incident in most jurisdictions, not merely shadow IT.
log_sources: CASB activity logs (Netskope / Defender for Cloud Apps)
Exchange message trace / email gateway logs
detection: Alert on DLP matches for PII classifiers where the destination is an AI-category unsanctioned application; auto-open a privacy incident with record counts.

name: Sustained low-and-slow egress to AI endpoints
description: Many small uploads to AI services across a long window, which individually fall under DLP thresholds but cumulatively represent substantial data loss.
log_sources: Web proxy / SWG logs (Zscaler / Netskope / Palo Alto)
CASB activity logs (Netskope / Defender for Cloud Apps)
detection: Aggregate bytes_out per user per AI destination over 7 to 30 days; alert on cumulative volume or on session counts far above peer-group norms, rather than per-event size.

name: Database or warehouse query results routed to an AI tool
description: A large query extract is followed by an upload of comparable size to an AI service — the warehouse-to-model exfiltration chain.
log_sources: Web proxy / SWG logs (Zscaler / Netskope / Palo Alto)
detection: Sequence rule: query returning more than N rows or MB, then within 30 minutes an AI-destination upload of similar magnitude by the same identity or host.

name: Corporate document shared into an AI tool via a public link
description: Rather than uploading, the user generates an anyone-with-the-link share and feeds the URL to an AI tool, which fetches the content — exfiltration by reference, invisible to upload DLP.
log_sources: Google Workspace admin & app audit logs
Web proxy / SWG logs (Zscaler / Netskope / Palo Alto)
detection: Correlate creation of anonymous sharing links with subsequent file fetches from AI provider ASNs, or with the link appearing in prompt bodies at the gateway.

name: Corporate data used to fine-tune an external model
description: A fine-tuning or custom-model job is created at an external provider using company data, permanently embedding proprietary information in a third-party model.
log_sources: Web proxy / SWG logs (Zscaler / Netskope / Palo Alto)
detection: Alert on calls to fine-tuning endpoints (/v1/fine_tuning/jobs and equivalents) from corporate networks, or on file-upload endpoints preceding them.

name: AI tool in the expense or procurement trail without security review
description: Card transactions, invoices, or vendor records show AI subscriptions that never passed vendor risk assessment — the business-system route to shadow AI discovery, which catches tools the network never sees.
detection: Match merchant names and MCC codes against an AI vendor dictionary; alert on spend where no entry exists in the vendor-risk register, then reconcile against proxy data.

name: Shadow AI tool authenticated with corporate SSO self-service
description: A user signs up to an AI SaaS with their corporate identity through social or SSO login, creating an enterprise-identity-linked tenant outside IT's knowledge.
log_sources: Google Workspace admin & app audit logs
CASB activity logs (Netskope / Defender for Cloud Apps)
detection: Alert on first-seen federated sign-ins where the relying party is an unregistered application and the identity domain is corporate; feed results into the SaaS register.

name: Prompt content containing internal identifiers observed in egress
description: Inline inspection of AI-bound requests reveals internal project codenames, customer IDs, or hostnames, confirming that real business context — not generic queries — is leaving.
log_sources: CASB activity logs (Netskope / Defender for Cloud Apps)
detection: Build a dictionary of internal codenames, customer ID formats, and FQDN patterns; match against AI-bound request bodies and alert with the matched terms for triage.

name: AI agent granted long-lived personal access token to a code host
description: A classic PAT or deploy key is minted for an AI tool, giving an unvetted service persistent repository access that outlives any session control.
detection: Alert on PAT or deploy-key creation whose name or user agent matches AI tooling, with broad scopes or no expiry; cross-check against the approved integration list.

name: Unmanaged AI container or image pulled to corporate infrastructure
description: An inference server image (vLLM, text-generation-webui, open-webui) is pulled from a public registry and run on corporate compute without review.
detection: Alert on image pulls matching AI inference-server patterns from public registries, and on pods exposing inference ports without an approved workload entry.

name: AI desktop application with filesystem access installed
description: A desktop AI client granted local file or disk access indexes corporate documents and ships them to its provider, bypassing network DLP entirely for indexed content.
log_sources: Web proxy / SWG logs (Zscaler / Netskope / Palo Alto)
detection: Alert on installation of AI desktop clients plus grants of full-disk or documents-folder access; correlate with sustained upload volume to the provider.

name: Blocked AI access attempts trending upward
description: A rising volume of blocked attempts to reach AI tools, read not as successful defence but as unmet demand that will route around the control if left unaddressed.
log_sources: Web proxy / SWG logs (Zscaler / Netskope / Palo Alto)
detection: Trend blocked AI-category events by user, department, and destination; report weekly and route the top requested tools into vendor assessment.

name: Shadow AI agent with write access to a production system
description: An unregistered agent performs mutating operations — record updates, ticket closures, configuration changes — in a production system, with no change control and no rollback owner.
detection: Flag write operations carrying agent-framework user agents or non-interactive cadence against production objects; alert immediately on any destructive verb.

name: AI tool reading CI-CD secrets or environment variables
description: An AI assistant or agent inside the pipeline enumerates environment variables or secret files, pulling build-time credentials into prompt context and provider logs.
detection: Alert on pipeline steps where AI tooling is invoked after secret injection, and on secrets-manager reads attributed to AI-assistant steps rather than deploy steps.

name: Shadow AI usage by a privileged or executive identity
description: Unsanctioned AI activity attributable to an admin, executive, or other high-value identity, where the blast radius of leaked context or a compromised session is disproportionate.
log_sources: CASB activity logs (Netskope / Defender for Cloud Apps)
detection: Join shadow AI activity with identity tier (Tier 0 admins, executives, board); alert on any unsanctioned AI session by these identities regardless of volume.
